claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among single-phase FCC Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni-derived alloys are governed by local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions set the activation-energy barriers for dislocation slip.
Reducing constituent count from quinary to quaternary to ternary decreases lattice distortion.
Decreased lattice distortion lowers the activation energy for dislocation slip.
Lower slip activation energy results in lower strength.
Composition changes alter local atomic configurations and the intensity of lattice strain fields.
Local lattice distortions are maximized in the equiatomic quinary alloy.
Greater lattice distortion in the equiatomic quinary alloy raises resistance to dislocation glide.
Quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower slip activation energies than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Quaternary and ternary alloys will exhibit smaller strain-rate sensitivity than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower overall strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
TEM will show dislocation structures that are less retarded by local strain fields in lower-component alloys.
The proposed constituent-count trend is limited to single-phase FCC alloys with matched thermomechanical processing histories.
Multiphase structures, secondary precipitates, or markedly different processing histories may invalidate the proposed trend.
